_note: Reviewer routing for [GP-Bot] PRs, consumed by .github/workflows/gpbot-pr-triage.yml.
Bot PRs arrive without a human owner. This file says which rotation owns the ticket and how to reach that rotation's holder on GitHub; it does not say who the holder is.
Editing it is a normal reviewable PR — that is the point of it being here rather than in workflow YAML.

There is deliberately no reviewer pool. @serve-bugs and @win-bugs are two-week on-call rotations carrying exactly one person at a time, so the Slack group already IS the answer to 'who looks at this': the workflow reads the current holder from usergroups.users.list when the PR opens, and a handoff needs no commit here.

The only hand-maintained part is githubLogins, because GitHub Actions cannot derive a GitHub login from a Slack user. It is keyed on work email rather than the Slack U0... id: Slack returns the email from users.info, `git log --format='%ae'` and `gh api users/<login>` corroborate it from the GitHub side, and an entry a reviewer can read is an entry a reviewer can check — an opaque id can only be trusted.
A missing entry costs one un-requested review, never a wrong one: the announcement still mentions the group, which is the on-call person. Add people as they join a rotation; never guess a login.
